decisions.quote: In Keysar et al (2003), the authors found that 71% of participants attempted to move a hidden object at least once when given a potentially ambiguous instruction, compared to 0% in the baseline condition, therefore failing to take into account the director’s perspective. We found 93% in the experimental condition and 14% in the baseline condition using raw error counts. We also found that people were more likely to hover over the distractor in the experimental condition than the baseline condition. Although there were a number of potentially concerning differences between our online version and the original version, it’s fair to say we replicated the original results.
decisions.location: PRIMARY PROJECT REPORT: keysar2003.pdf, Discussion > Summary of Replication Attempt (line 587); also PRIMARY PROJECT FILE raw_data.csv, row keysar2003 (line 225)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree on a 'successful' replication outcome for Keysar, Lin, & Barr (2003) Study 1 (blind coding lacked a supporting quote). Both the included primary replication report (keysar2003.pdf, which concludes 'it’s fair to say we replicated the original results' after finding 93% vs. 14% error rates and significant distractor hover-time interaction) and the project dataset raw_data.csv (keysar2003: same_dir=yes, prop: 13/14 vs. 2/14, replicated_instructor_code=1, replicated_report_code=1) confirm a successful replication.
